correctness.rationale: The paired squared-pole rational identity has a cubic numerator P in z² and no real roots or pole cancellations. Exact cubic and coefficient-quadratic discriminants yield all nondegenerate sign chambers and double-root boundaries, with positive masses. At the unique critical point P factors exactly as a cubic power, giving one upper-plane triple zero. An explicit nonzero Jacobian and exact boundary-width asymptotic give the 3/2 cusp. A standalone exact symbolic checker reproduces critical identities; numerical cases are not used to prove all parameter values.
